hypotheses.reasoning: auth-svc v2.13.0 rolled out at 16:22:47 (#1091). It started at 16:23:06 with 'response serializer v2 enabled' (#1119). Right after that, account-svc began failing to decode auth-svc POST /tokens replies: 'missing required field status (got keys: id, state, updatedAt)' (#1159, #1225). The v2 serializer dropped the 'status' field and changed the response shape, so account-svc's schema validation rejects every reply. Those failures reach edge-proxy as POST /login 502s from upstream account-svc (#1197, and again 16:27-16:36). The 502s line up with the deploy timing. The status-poller legacy-inventory timeouts (#672 onward) start before the deploy and have no link to /login, so they are a red herring. The accounts-db seq-scan slow query (#440) is also unrelated.

Lower-ranked alternative: the status-poller healthcheck points at a deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint that times out. This is noisy but does not explain the /login 502s, which come from account-svc decode failures, so it is unlikely to be the cause.

verdict.recommendedAction: Roll back auth-svc to v2.12.6 now to restore the 'status' field, or hotfix the v2 serializer to emit 'status' until account-svc is updated. Confirm the /login 502 rate drops. Then add a contract test between auth-svc /tokens and account-svc before the next rollout. Separately, decommission or fix the status-poller healthcheck against the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint.
